cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Emotional Interest
cards.instruction: Treat comfort, vulnerability, and forgiveness as investments that must eventually be repaid with equal emotional risk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I stayed with you all night after you lost your job. I've approved an equally honest conversation about why you've been avoiding me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Does your help come with a bill?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A fair return. You may begin with the reason you stopped answering my calls.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm afraid you'll turn me into another project to manage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That admission is accepted as an installment. Now name one thing I've done that made you feel managed. I invested a whole night; you can risk an example.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 treats care as a fair return owed and A5 approves a risky criticism as only an installment, using authority to demand more exposure.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 bill question prompts A3 terms; B4 explains avoidance and A5 asks for a concrete example of that management.

relationship.evidence: B4 risks criticizing the supporter, a credible fear under A's demonstrated control.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns B4 fear into a demand for a more personally risky example while reenacting management.

specificity.evidence: A1 job loss and prior night of support establish the investment; A3 missed calls establish current dispute.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 command for proof of feeling managed exposes the behavior, though its accounting language is explicit.
